tier: ISP proxies, billed per IP by term

free_tier.stated: No free tier is stated. The cheapest purchase is one address for 24 hours at USD 1.80; the same address costs USD 2.70 for 30 days, USD 2.55 for 60 days and USD 2.40 for 90 days. Included in every plan, in the vendor's words: 500K+ unique IPs in 31+ countries, country, state and city-level targeting, customizable plans, SOCKS5 support, UDP and TCP connections, IP replacement, unlimited sessions, 24/7 support.
free_tier.notes: The 24-hour term is the shortest and cheapest unit, which the vendor describes as a test with no long-term commitment; it is the same product at its shortest term, not a free trial.

per_object_cap.notes: The unit sold is one IP address with a port, a username and a password, held for the term purchased.

retention.stated: not applicable: a rented address, not stored bytes
retention.notes: The only clock is the rental term, priced at 24 hours, 30, 60 and 90 days. The vendor describes the address as reserved for the buyer: Dedicated IP Pool, keep the same IP address as long as needed.

egress.terms: The product page adds unlimited sessions and included traffic with fair usage protection for high-volume use cases; the pricing page states unlimited threads, and its page description states unlimited bandwidth.
egress.free_allowance: traffic included with the per-IP price; no byte figure published and the fair-use clause is unquantified

interface_detail: The endpoint is a proxy address with a port, a username and a password, over HTTP(S) or SOCKS5, with UDP and TCP connections. The vendor runs a self-service dashboard and an HTTP API at apid.iproyal.com, whose documentation sample is GET https://apid.iproyal.com/v1/reseller/balance with an apiToken. The schema's interface enum has no proxy-protocol token, so rest indexes the API and the proxy protocols are stated here.
tooling: Any client that takes a proxy address with credentials: curl --proxy, Python requests with proxies=, a headless browser with proxy settings, or a SOCKS5-capable client. The vendor states a self-service dashboard with IP whitelist management and API access; its documentation sample calls GET https://apid.iproyal.com/v1/reseller/balance with an apiToken. Checking an issued address's registration takes a whois or RIPE lookup on that address.
chaining: One purchased address in front of the outbound leg of a Workers AI gateway or a crawler, where a stable source address per request matters. It carries no storage and no compute, so it sits beside compute and egress records rather than replacing either.

limits.value: no published request-rate or concurrency figure; the vendor states unlimited threads and unlimited sessions
one dedicated address per purchased slot, so all of a slot's traffic shares one IP's reputation; the vendor sells IP replacement as the remedy

limits_note: Zero session limits is prose naming no vocabulary kind: it says the vendor caps neither session length nor session count, which removes a shaping constraint rather than creating one. The fair-use clause behind included traffic is the one qualifier that could become a ceiling, and it publishes no number.
binding_note: The vendor states unlimited sessions and unlimited threads with traffic included per IP, so no request-rate, count or byte ceiling of the vocabulary is published. Cost scales with the number of addresses held, USD 1.80 to USD 2.70 per address per term, and the one qualifier that could become a ceiling is the provider, which publishes no number.

identity_cost.detail: Payment methods listed: Visa, Mastercard, PayPal, Discover, Amex, Alipay and crypto. Sign-up offers Google, LinkedIn or a form, with an hCaptcha. The KYC policy screens the IP address, email and other data at registration and applies identity verification at purchase, which it says ensures unrestricted access to all services; the product page states the vendor gets to know customers before providing full access to ISP proxies. Whether the purchase-stage identity verification asks for an identity document is not stated.

reliability_note: One dedicated address carries all of a slot's traffic, so a block follows the address; the vendor's stated remedy is IP replacement. Stated uptime is 99.9% and stated success rate up to 99.99%; neither is measured. The KYC policy states access can be suspended for any customer, usually after a request for an explanation of usage.
confidence_note: Documented: the per-IP prices (USD 1.80 for 24 hours, USD 2.70 for 30 days, USD 2.55 for 60 days, USD 2.40 for 90 days), the feature list, the per-IP billing sentence with the provider qualifier, the payment methods and the KYC stages are stated on the vendor's product, pricing and KYC pages. Nothing about an issued address is measured: measured needs one purchased address, a whois or RIPE lookup of its registration class and AS, and a byte and request count through it.

evidence.proved: The FAQ, read directly: ISP proxies use IP addresses registered to consumer internet service providers. These IPs are hosted on data center servers. The same page states every ISP proxy belongs only to you, unlimited sessions, 500K+ unique IPs in 31+ countries, country/state/city targeting, SOCKS5 support, UDP and TCP, IP replacement, 99.9% uptime and a self-service dashboard.
Same page: unlimited threads, unlimited bandwidth claimed, and the FAQ answer giving an IP address, port, username and password as what the buyer receives.

The price ladder and payment methods as recorded by the research pass of 2026-10-24: $1.80 per proxy for 24 hours, $2.70 for 30 days, $2.55 for 60 days, $2.40 for 90 days; Visa, Mastercard, PayPal, Alipay or crypto. Passed on from that read, not re-observed by this record's raw fetch, which returned no dollar figures.

price_per_tb_month: no per-TB figure exists: the vendor bills per IP with traffic included. The comparable numbers are USD 1.80 per address per 24 hours, USD 2.70 per address per 30 days, USD 2.55 at 60 days and USD 2.40 at 90 days.
notes: The unit sold is one dedicated IP address with a port, a username and a password, held for 24 hours, 30, 60 or 90 days. The vendor states the addresses are registered to consumer internet service providers and hosted on data center servers. No sample address, no free trial and no list of announcing ASNs or prefixes is published on the product or pricing page, so the registration class of an address cannot be checked before purchase; the shortest term, USD 1.80 for 24 hours, is the lowest-cost unit on which a whois or RIPE lookup of an issued address is possible. Per-object cap and retention do not apply to an address.
